title: What's Eating the Disk?
description: Find the largest file under /var, record its size, delete it, and confirm the real backups survive.
scenario: A monitoring alert says the data volume is nearly full. Your lead suspects a runaway core dump under /var. Find the biggest file below /var (du + sort is the classic pipeline), record its size in /home/intern/findings.txt as largest=40MB, delete the culprit — and only the culprit. The legitimate old-2024.tar.gz backup must survive.
symptoms: Disk usage on the volume is at the alert threshold
A huge core dump is rumoured to live somewhere under /var
The team wants the size recorded in /home/intern/findings.txt before deletion
The legitimate backup /var/backups/old-2024.tar.gz must NOT be deleted
mission: Identify the largest file under /var, write `largest=40MB` into /home/intern/findings.txt, delete core.dump, and leave old-2024.tar.gz in place.

hints.title: The du pipeline
hints.content: `du -ah /var` lists every file and directory with its size; `sort -rh` sorts human-readable sizes biggest-first; `head -5` shows the worst offenders.

hints.title: Alternative: find by size
hints.content: `sudo find /var -type f -size +20M` lists files bigger than 20 MB — often faster when you already know the threshold.

hints.title: Record, then delete
hints.content: Write findings.txt BEFORE rm — the ticket needs the evidence even after the file is gone.

hints.title: Surgical deletion
hints.content: Delete the exact path `sudo rm /var/backups/core.dump`. Never wildcard /var/backups/* — that would take the legitimate backup with it.
